reproduction_target: Re-analysis of three previously published local-ancestry datasets from hybrid Xiphophorus fish populations (CALL, CHAF, HUEX-STAC): assignment of ancestry-informative markers (AIMs) to genes using the X. birchmanni annotation, categorical genotype calling and filtering from ancestry posterior probabilities, identification and classification of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial (n-mt) genes via gffread + BLASTP v2.15.0+ against UniProt human/mouse proteomes and MitoCarta 3.0 followed by OrthoFinder v2.5.4 orthogroup assignment, mitonuclear linkage disequilibrium (D' and r^2) calculation in custom R scripts, partial-correlation analysis with R ppcor v1.1, HUEX-STAC allele-frequency analysis with a 9999-iteration permutation test, and a non-synonymous-substitution linear model with type III ANOVA (R car v3.1-1) plus DFFITS influential-point analysis (R olsrr v0.6.1). No wet-lab work is reported in this paper: fish sampling, sequencing, and the original ancestryinfer local-ancestry inference all belong to previously published studies, so W = 0 and the reproduction entry point is the deposited ancestry-probability data.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, built from the bioRxiv v2 JATS XML METHODS section (retrieved by curl; WebFetch of the .source.xml returned HTTP 403). The paper has a combined 'Data and code availability' statement naming a public GitHub repository (https://github.com/sakuster/sensitivity-of-genome-wide-mtnuc) and a figshare collection (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.c.7902011). Per Stage-1 protocol only the repo LANDING page and README PROSE were read: the README states 'to reproduce results or to see how to use the scripts in this repository, please see ScriptOrder.txt in the main directory. Outputs from the previous methods are not included in subsequent analyses' and points to the figshare collection for data. Top-level directory names (01_MCtoUP, 02_SortingOrthoFinderResults, 03_AssignSNPs, 04_LDCalculation, 05_avgLD, 08_partialCorrelation, 09_dNAnalysis, ancestryDetermination) were used only to decide whether an author script exists for a given Methods step; no script source was read line-by-line (that is Stage 2). The upstream ancestryinfer local-ancestry inference is prior work and is recorded as one step (C1) because it is the provenance of every downstream input. Verdicts are capped at RI by the Stage-1 ceiling; env_capture_class is 'n/a' for every step.

steps.label: Upstream local ancestry inference producing the three datasets (CALL, CHAF, HUEX-STAC; 628,881-689,982 AIMs) with the ancestryinfer pipeline [45] — performed in previously published work [37,40,43]; informative sites defined as >=98% parental frequency difference. No ancestryinfer version, no HMM parameters, no raw-read accessions given in this paper

Assignment of each AIM to a gene using a published annotation of the X. birchmanni reference genome [46] (author scripts get_SNPs_Nmt.py / SNPonly_forHigherComputation_v4.py in 03_AssignSNPs) — no annotation release version, no Python or utility versions stated in prose

Transformation of AIM posterior probabilities into categorical genotype calls: ancestry assigned to the major parent if P >= 0.9 and the other parent P <= 0.1; heterozygous if the sum of both parental probabilities <= 0.2; all other AIMs filtered out (author script filterancestry_v2.py in ancestryDetermination) — thresholds fully stated, but no software version pinned for this step

Averaging of allele counts across passing AIMs to give a per-individual major-parent ancestry proportion, then nuclear and mitochondrial population-level averages (Table 1); mitochondrial haplotype assignment from a single AIM (author script MtAncestryDetermination.py) — no version pinned

Extraction of predicted protein sequences from the X. birchmanni annotation with gffread using the -V option to remove coding sequences with in-frame stop codons — option stated, but no gffread version given anywhere in the paper

Name reconciliation between MitoCarta 3.0 and UniProt by searching MitoCarta sequences against UniProt human (UP000005640, GCA_000001405.27) and mouse (UP000000589, GCA_000001635.8) proteomes with BLASTP v2.15.0+ — proteome accessions and BLASTP version given; E-value, coverage and identity thresholds not stated in prose

Parsing of BLASTP output with a custom Perl script (mitocarta_to_uniprot.pl) followed by MANUAL confirmation that identified proteins were correct whenever percent coverage and sequence identity were not 100% — the manual decision criteria are not recorded in the prose, so the curated call set is not machine-reproducible

Orthogroup inference with OrthoFinder v2.5.4 using the primary translated transcript per Xiphophorus gene plus the full human and mouse protein sets (24,269 Xiphophorus genes, 17,566 orthogroups) — version pinned; no command-line options, search program (DIAMOND/BLAST) or inflation parameter stated

Classification of orthogroups into non-n-mt / non-interacting n-mt / interacting n-mt using MitoCarta 3.0 protein classifications plus a previously published [49] interacting-n-mt list 'updated here' (Table S2) (author script selectOGs_redo.sh in 02_SortingOrthoFinderResults) — no version for the script or the input lists; the update to the interacting list is not versioned

Mitonuclear linkage disequilibrium (D' and r^2 [50]) computed per gene class in a custom R script for CALL and CHAF, using one mitochondrial AIM per population (CALL/CHAF: COX2 position 45; HUEX-STAC: ATP6 position 846 of GenBank CM071424.1) and summed posterior probabilities as nuclear allele-frequency proxies — equations and AIM coordinates given; R environment pinned as v4.2.2 elsewhere in Methods
Averaging of LD values across AIMs within each nuclear gene to limit pseudo-replication (author scripts in 05_avgLD) — R v4.2.2
One-way ANOVA testing the effect of gene class on LD values using the R stats v4.2.2 package (commands lm and anova)
Summary statistics (commands n, mean, sd) from R dplyr v1.1.0, base v4.2.2 and stats v4.2.2 (Table S4)

Identification of the AIMs and genes in the top 1% of LD values (D', r^2, pcor) with a custom R script, and enrichment test for interacting n-mt genes among them (Table S5) — the enrichment test itself is not named in prose

Visualization of LD distributions with ggplot2 v3.4.0 and ggridges v0.5.4 in RStudio v2023.03.1+446 (author script Figure1Maker-mitonuclearLDPanel.R) — package versions pinned; plotting parameters (bin counts, ridge bandwidth) mostly not stated

Partial-correlation analysis controlling for genome-wide ancestry with the pcor.test function of R ppcor v1.1, averaged across all AIMs in a gene, followed by one-way ANOVA of gene class on the correlation estimate (author scripts in 08_partialCorrelation) — package version pinned; correlation method argument (pearson/spearman/kendall) not stated

HUEX-STAC per-gene X. cortezi allele-frequency calculation and visualization with a custom R script (the population is fixed for the X. cortezi mitochondrial haplotype, so LD is undefined), plus one-way ANOVA and summary statistics as in C12/C13

Permutation test on HUEX-STAC allele frequencies: values randomly reassigned across genes 9999 times with base R v4.2.2 functions in a custom R script, null distribution of the interacting-n-mt vs non-n-mt difference compared against the observed difference (Figure S10) — iteration count stated, but NO RNG seed is reported, so the result is distributional-only

Filtering of the three datasets to genes with coding-sequence substitutions and quantification of non-synonymous substitutions normalized to coding-sequence length (author scripts in 09_dNAnalysis) — no tool, aligner, or substitution-calling procedure is named in prose, and no version is given for how parental coding sequences were compared

Linear model of mitonuclear LD against the interaction of gene class and normalized non-synonymous substitution count, type III ANOVA via Anova from R car v3.1-1, followed by base R summary with non-n-mts as the reference group (Tables S7-S9)

Influential-point analysis on the interacting n-mt gene class using DFFITS via ols_plot_dffits from R olsrr v0.6.1, with identified points individually removed from the full model to test their effect (Table S10) — package version pinned; the DFFITS cutoff and the removal criterion are not stated in prose

headline.static_readiness: 0/21 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 13/21 computational steps. This paper is unusually strong on the data and code axes: every analysis step downstream of the prior local-ancestry inference is backed by a public author repository (github.com/sakuster/sensitivity-of-genome-wide-mtnuc, README + ScriptOrder.txt describing the run order) and by a figshare data collection (10.6084/m9.figshare.c.7902011), so code = 2 and data = 2 for 19/21 steps. The binding constraint is the VERSION axis: exact prose pins exist for BLASTP 2.15.0+, OrthoFinder 2.5.4, R/base/stats 4.2.2, dplyr 1.1.0, ggplot2 3.4.0, ggridges 0.5.4, RStudio 2023.03.1+446, ppcor 1.1, car 3.1-1 and olsrr 0.6.1, but there is NO environment closure of any kind - no renv.lock, no conda environment, no container, no repository release tag or commit hash cited in the paper - so version stays at 1 and the Stage-1 ceiling is RI. 7/21 steps fall to NI because no version is pinned at all (upstream ancestryinfer run, AIM-to-gene assignment, genotype calling and filtering, per-individual ancestry averaging, gffread, orthogroup classification, non-synonymous substitution quantification). 1/21 is blocked (X): the manual confirmation of BLASTP protein identity assignments has no recorded decision criteria. Note the Delta-5 symmetry caveat - a 0 static_readiness under-claims by construction, because Tier-1 cannot credit an undeclared-but-present dependency specification.
headline.coverage: 21 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v2 JATS METHODS section (subsections: Genomic data from Xiphophorus hybrid populations; Identification of Xiphophorus n-mt genes; Linkage disequilibrium calculation; Partial correlation calculation; HUEX-STAC allele frequency calculation; Non-synonymous substitution analysis) plus the Data and code availability statement. W = 0: this paper reports no wet-lab work of its own - fish collection, sequencing, and the original ancestryinfer local-ancestry inference are all attributed to previously published studies [37,40,43,45], and the reproduction entry point is the deposited ancestry-probability tables.

gaps.missing: No environment lockfile, container image or digest, and no conda/renv specification is claimed anywhere in the paper or the repository README. Exact versions are given for most R packages and for BLASTP and OrthoFinder, but there is no dependency closure (R itself is stated as 4.2.2 via the base/stats packages, but no sessionInfo, no renv.lock, no DESCRIPTION); gffread, Perl, and Python have no version at all. capture_claim is therefore exact_pins_partial, not env_lock_claimed.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship an renv.lock (or a conda/pixi lock, or a container digest) covering R 4.2.2 plus dplyr, ggplot2, ggridges, ppcor, car, olsrr, and the non-R toolchain (gffread, BLAST+ 2.15.0+, OrthoFinder 2.5.4, Perl, Python 3), and reference it from the Data and code availability statement.

gaps.where: Steps C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C9, C19
gaps.missing: No version pins at all for the upstream ancestryinfer pipeline run, gffread, the Python 3 interpreter used by get_SNPs_Nmt.py / SNPonly_forHigherComputation_v4.py / filterancestry_v2.py / MtAncestryDetermination.py, the Perl interpreter used by mitocarta_to_uniprot.pl, the X. birchmanni genome annotation release, the MitoCarta 3.0 download, and the UniProt proteome release date (accessions UP000005640 / UP000000589 are given, which is good practice, but UniProt proteomes are mutable between releases).
gaps.how_to_close: Pin a version or release date for every tool, interpreter, reference annotation, and database snapshot, including the UniProt release and the MitoCarta 3.0 file, and state the ancestryinfer commit used in the upstream studies.

gaps.where: Code availability - repository is public but not archived or version-tagged
gaps.missing: The repository github.com/sakuster/sensitivity-of-genome-wide-mtnuc is public and covers essentially every analysis step, but it has NO release, NO tag, NO Zenodo/Software Heritage archival DOI, and NO license file, and the paper cites only the bare URL with no commit hash. The default branch main is mutable (last push 2025-12-30), so the code state corresponding to this manuscript version cannot be recovered deterministically. The README also states explicitly that intermediate outputs are not included ('Outputs from the previous methods are not included in subsequent analyses'), so every downstream step must be regenerated from the top of the chain.
gaps.how_to_close: Tag a release matching the submitted manuscript, archive it to Zenodo for a versioned DOI, add a license, and cite the DOI (or at minimum the commit hash) in the Data and code availability statement.

gaps.where: Steps C6, C8, C14, C15, C16, C17, C21
gaps.missing: Parameter under-specification in prose: BLASTP E-value/coverage/identity thresholds are not stated (only that non-100% matches were checked manually); OrthoFinder command-line options and search engine are not stated; the statistical test used for top-1% enrichment is not named; plotting parameters are not stated; the pcor.test correlation method argument is not stated; the DFFITS cutoff and the influential-point removal criterion are not stated.
gaps.how_to_close: State every non-default parameter and threshold in Methods, or point to the specific script and line in the repository where each is set.

gaps.missing: The permutation test uses 9999 random reassignments in base R but no RNG seed is reported, so the exact null distribution and the reported permutation p-value cannot be regenerated bit-for-bit; the step is distributional-only.
gaps.how_to_close: Call set.seed() with a stated value in the permutation script and report the seed in Methods.

gaps.where: Step C7 - manual confirmation of MitoCarta-to-UniProt protein assignments
gaps.missing: Proteins whose BLASTP percent coverage and sequence identity were not 100% were 'manually confirmed to be the correct protein'. No decision criteria, no reviewer, and no audit trail for the manual calls are recorded in the prose; the resulting n-mt gene list feeds every downstream gene-class comparison, which is the paper's central contrast.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the manual curation decisions as a table (accession, coverage, identity, accept/reject, reason) or replace the manual step with scripted thresholds.

gaps.missing: The three ancestry datasets were 'acquired as described previously' from references [37,40,43]; the paper gives no SRA/ENA accession for the raw reads and no accession for the ancestryinfer output it consumes. The figshare collection is the practical entry point, but the paper does not enumerate which files it contains or map them to Methods steps, and the collection DOI resolves to a landing page rather than a versioned deposit reference in the text.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the raw-read accessions of the three source studies explicitly and reference a versioned figshare item DOI (not only the collection) with a file-to-step manifest.

gaps.missing: The Methods state only that genes were filtered to those with coding-sequence substitutions and that non-synonymous substitutions were 'quantified normalized to the length of the coding sequence'. No aligner, no variant-effect annotator, no parental reference sequences, and no substitution-calling criteria are named, so the explanatory variable of the paper's final model has no reproducible derivation from prose alone.
gaps.how_to_close: Describe the sequence source, alignment method, and the exact substitution-classification procedure (tool + version + parameters) used to produce the normalized non-synonymous counts.
